yuki: Noticed docs PR #5102 has several inconsistencies for the /generate batch examples. The curl and python snippets use "max_tokens" (legacy) while our runtime and OpenAPI use "max_new_tokens". Also the stop sequences are shown as a single string "\n" rather than an array ["\n"]. CI snippet-runner fails on that.
omar: Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5102
lina: Oof. Which files are affected? I can take a pass if someone points me to the examples.
yuki: docs/reference/generate.md (curl + python + node examples), samples/batch.md, and api-ref/generate.yaml example payload.
omar: The problematic curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-2","max_tokens":50,"stop":"\n","inputs":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"},{"role":"user","content":"How are you?"}]}'
```
This should be normalized to:
```
{"model":"redwood-2","max_new_tokens":50,"stop":["\n"],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"},{"role":"user","content":"How are you?"}]}
```
Note: inputs->messages and max_tokens->max_new_tokens and stop->array.
lina: I'll update the examples. We intentionally allowed "inputs" previously for legacy compatibility, but docs should show the canonical shape and optionally mention legacy aliases in a short note.
yuki: Also, the python snippet uses `client.generate(input=...)` which the Python SDK removed last quarter in favor of `messages=` and keyword `max_new_tokens`. Test runner flags the mismatch.
omar: Can we add a tiny compatibility note in generate.md: "legacy: inputs -> still accepted by runtime but examples use messages for clarity"? That should reduce future confusion.
lina: I'll add that and a brief paragraph about stop formats (string vs array) and explain precedence rules: if stop is scalar treat as single token sequence. Also will update api-ref/generate.yaml example to omit legacy fields and set nullable optional timeout_ms to null in example rather than a number, since that caused a separate lint failure last week.
docs-bot: build-docs #1310 started for branch docs/fix-generate-examples (triggered by lina)
yuki: One more—node snippet had streaming example that emits chunks using `role`/`content` envelope, but our streaming contract uses `type` and `delta` inside SSE events for /chat. Let's align the generate streaming example to the chat-stream contract, and call out the slight difference for non-chat models.
lina: Good catch. I'll rework node/python streaming examples to emit events with `event: message` and payload {"type":"delta","delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"..."}} so it matches the stream parser in the SDK.
omar: After you push, can you run the snippet tests locally? I can review the PR and add a CHANGELOG line referencing snip-051.
lina: Pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/9f7d2b3. Updated examples, added a small unit in snippet-linter to detect legacy max_tokens and inputs in example bodies, and added docs/changes.md entry.
docs-bot: build-docs #1310 succeeded for branch docs/fix-generate-examples
yuki: Ran the snippet CI on that commit — all green here. Thanks @lina and @omar. Closing out the thread.
